events.text: Giuseppe Piazzi discovered Ceres, the first object found in the asteroid belt and now classed as a dwarf planet, from the Palermo Astronomical Observatory in Sicily.
NASA's Stardust spacecraft flew past Comet Wild 2 and collected dust from its coma for return to Earth.
Kathryn Aurora Gray, aged 10, discovered the supernova SN 2010lt in the galaxy UGC 3378 with Paul Gray and David J. Lane. She became the youngest person known to have found a supernova at the time.
Stephen P. Synnott discovered Portia, one of the inner moons of Uranus, in images taken by Voyager 2.
China's Chang'e 4 lander touched down in Von Kármán crater, becoming the first spacecraft to land on the far side of the Moon.
NASA's Spirit rover landed inside Gusev crater on Mars.
The Kepler space telescope team announced its first main results. The initial planet discoveries were all short-period planets.
Mike Brown, Chad Trujillo and David Rabinowitz discovered the dwarf planet Eris in images taken in 2003 with the Samuel Oschin Schmidt telescope at Palomar Observatory.
NASA released a new Hubble image of the Pillars of Creation in the Eagle Nebula, along with a panoramic view of the Andromeda Galaxy showing more than 100 million stars.
William Herschel discovered NGC 2023, a reflection nebula in Orion near the Horsehead Nebula.
Hubble released a sharp image of the Ring Nebula, a cylinder of gas from a dying star seen almost end-on.
NASA announced the 1,000th confirmed exoplanet discovered by the Kepler space telescope.
Galileo Galilei wrote a letter containing the first mention of the moons of Jupiter, which he had seen through his telescope.
The first Hubble Frontier Fields image showed the galaxy cluster Abell 2744 and some of the faintest and youngest galaxies detected up to that time.
The ALeRCE automated classification system discovered SN 2020oi, a Type Ic supernova in the spiral galaxy Messier 100.
Galileo Galilei died at his villa in Arcetri near Florence, where he had lived under house arrest since 1634.
ESA's Gaia spacecraft reached its planned orbit around the Sun-Earth L2 Lagrange point, about three weeks after launch.
NASA deployed and locked the second side wing of the James Webb Space Telescope's primary mirror, completing the observatory's structural deployment in space.
Caroline Herschel died in Hanover at age 97. Working with her brother William, she discovered comets and nebulae, including a companion galaxy of Andromeda now called Messier 110.
Alicia Soderberg and Edo Berger, and independently Albert Kong and Tom Maccarone, used the Swift satellite to detect the explosion that became supernova SN 2008D in the spiral galaxy NGC 2770.
Harold Webb and Herbert Kauffman of Project Diana detected the first radar echo bounced off the Moon.
Astronomers released a Hubble image of Betelgeuse, the first direct image of the surface of a star other than the Sun. It showed a hot spot on the star.
William Herschel discovered Titania and Oberon, the two largest moons of Uranus, on the same night.
Diamond miners in the Transvaal are thought to have been the first to see the Great January Comet of 1910, already bright enough to see with the naked eye before dawn.
Comet McNaught passed perihelion, its closest point to the Sun. It reached an estimated magnitude of minus 5.5 over the next two days.
Galileo Galilei saw all four of Jupiter's large moons at once for the first time.
Stephen P. Synnott discovered Desdemona, a small inner moon of Uranus, in images taken by Voyager 2.
Hubble observed Eta Carinae, an unstable star about 4 million times brighter and 150 times more massive than the Sun.
ESA's Huygens probe landed on Titan, Saturn's largest moon, after descending through its thick atmosphere.
The Hubble Deep Field image was released. It contained at least 1,500 galaxies at various stages of development.
Kōichi Itagaki discovered SN 2018gv, a Type Ia supernova in the spiral galaxy NGC 2525.
Charles Messier added the star cluster M41 to his catalog, describing it as a cluster of stars below Sirius.
William Herschel discovered the planetary nebula NGC 2392, now known as the Eskimo Nebula, while observing from Slough in England.
Clyde Tombaugh, the astronomer who discovered Pluto, died in Las Cruces, New Mexico, at age 90.
NASA launched the New Horizons spacecraft, which flew past Pluto in July 2015.
Richard J. Terrile discovered Cordelia, a small inner moon of Uranus, in images taken by Voyager 2.
Steve Fossey and four undergraduate students at the University of London Observatory spotted a bright new star in the galaxy Messier 82. It was the supernova SN 2014J.
Pierre Gassendi was born in Champtercier, Provence. In 1631 he became the first person to observe a planet crossing the Sun, watching the transit of Mercury that Kepler had predicted.
Earth received the final signal from Pioneer 10, then about 80 astronomical units away.
Amateur astronomer Jay McNeil of Paducah, Kentucky, discovered a new nebula near M78 with a 3-inch telescope. It is now known as McNeil's Nebula.
Voyager 2 made its closest approach to Uranus, passing about 81,500 kilometers above the cloud tops. The flyby revealed 11 previously unknown moons and two more rings.
The James Webb Space Telescope fired its thrusters for a final course correction that placed it into its planned orbit around the Sun-Earth L2 point, about 1.5 million kilometers from Earth.
The Infrared Astronomical Satellite, IRAS, was launched. It became the first space telescope to survey the entire night sky at infrared wavelengths.
The 200-inch Hale Telescope at Palomar Observatory saw first light under the direction of Edwin Hubble. Its first image showed NGC 2261, known as Hubble's Variable Nebula.
Galileo Galilei plotted a point in his drawings that matches the position of Neptune on that night. He had recorded a similar point on 28 December 1612.
Johannes Hevelius was born. He spent four years charting the Moon and published Selenographia, which earned him the title of founder of lunar topography.
Yoji Hirose discovered SN 2002ap, a Type Ic supernova in the spiral galaxy Messier 74.
NASA ended the Spitzer Space Telescope mission after more than 16 years of infrared observations, far beyond its planned two and a half years.
Alvan Graham Clark first observed Sirius B, the faint companion of Sirius, while testing an 18.5-inch refractor built for Dearborn Observatory.
William Herschel discovered the planetary nebula NGC 1535 in the constellation Eridanus.

The James Webb Space Telescope's NIRCam captured light from the star HD 84406 in Ursa Major through all 18 primary mirror segments, the telescope's first view of a star. NASA released the mosaic on 11 February.
source: NASA Webb blog: Photons Received: Webb Sees Its First Star, 18 Times

events.text: Johann Elert Bode discovered the globular cluster M53 early in the morning and described it as a rather conspicuous nebula.
Edward Charles Pickering died in Cambridge, Massachusetts. He directed the Harvard College Observatory and established the Harvard Photometry, the first great photometric star catalog.
Clyde Tombaugh, who later discovered Pluto, was born in Streator, Illinois.
Maarten Schmidt worked out that the spectrum of the radio source 3C 273 showed hydrogen lines with a large redshift, leading to the identification of the first known quasar.

Donald Lynden-Bell died at his home in Cambridge, England. In 1969 he proposed that quasars are powered by supermassive black holes, and he shared the first Kavli Prize in Astrophysics with Maarten Schmidt.
William Herschel discovered the planetary nebula NGC 3242, later nicknamed the Ghost of Jupiter, and cataloged it as H IV.27.
NASA launched Stardust to fly past Comet Wild 2 and collect dust from it. Its capsule returned more than 10,000 comet particles to Utah in 2006.
Fritz Zwicky, the astronomer who found evidence for dark matter and studied supernovae with Walter Baade, died in Pasadena, California.
Halley's Comet reached perihelion, passing about 87.8 million kilometers from the Sun.
The ESA and NASA Solar Orbiter spacecraft launched on an Atlas V rocket from Cape Canaveral, Florida.
Space Shuttle Discovery launched on Hubble's second servicing mission. Astronauts installed the STIS spectrograph and the NICMOS near-infrared camera.
The LIGO team announced the first direct detection of gravitational waves, produced by the merger of two black holes and recorded on 14 September 2015.
source: LIGO Caltech: Gravitational waves detected 100 years after Einstein's prediction

events.text: NASA's NEAR Shoemaker spacecraft touched down on the asteroid Eros at about 6.4 kilometers per hour, just south of a feature named Himeros.
Galileo Galilei arrived in Rome to face charges of heresy before the Inquisition for advocating the Copernican theory that the Earth moves around the Sun.
source: History.com: Galileo arrives in Rome to face charges of heresy

events.text: John Louis Emil Dreyer was born in Copenhagen. He compiled the New General Catalog of nebulae and star clusters, whose NGC numbers are still used to name galaxies and nebulae.
Fritz Zwicky was born in Varna, Bulgaria. He went on to find evidence for dark matter in 1933 and, with Walter Baade, proposed supernovae as a distinct class of stellar explosion.
Voyager 1 took the Pale Blue Dot image of Earth from about 6 billion kilometers from the Sun.
Galileo Galilei was born in Pisa, Italy.
William Herschel discovered the Cat's Eye Nebula, a planetary nebula in the constellation Draco.
Pierre Méchain discovered the Owl Nebula. Charles Messier added it to his catalog a few weeks later.
Gerard Kuiper discovered Miranda, a moon of Uranus, using the 82-inch Otto Struve Telescope at McDonald Observatory.
Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille discovered the spiral galaxy M83 while observing from the Cape of Good Hope.
Clyde Tombaugh pinpointed Pluto. Lowell Observatory announced the discovery on 13 March.
Nicolaus Copernicus was born in Toruń, in Royal Prussia.
Charles Messier discovered the open star cluster M47. A sign error in his recorded position was traced in 1959 by T.F. Morris, who showed the cluster is NGC 2422.
George Smoot was born in Yukon, Florida. He later shared the 2006 Nobel Prize in Physics for measurements of the microwave background radiation made with NASA's COBE satellite.
George Ellery Hale died in Pasadena, California. He built four major telescopes and is honored by the 200-inch Hale Telescope at Palomar Observatory.
William Herschel discovered the spiral galaxy NGC 3521 in the constellation Leo.
Pierre Janssen was born in Paris. In 1868 he found a new yellow line in the solar spectrum that was later traced to helium.
NASA announced that its Spitzer Space Telescope, with help from ground-based telescopes, had found seven Earth-size planets around the star TRAPPIST-1, about 40 light-years away in Aquarius.
source: NASA JPL: NASA Telescope Reveals Largest Batch of Earth-Size, Habitable-Zone Planets Around Single Star

events.text: The Kamiokande II, IMB and Baksan detectors recorded a burst of neutrinos from Supernova 1987A, a few hours before its visible light reached Earth.
Antony Hewish, Jocelyn Bell Burnell and colleagues published the discovery of the first radio pulsar, PSR B1919+21, in the journal Nature.

Ian Shelton and Oscar Duhalde discovered Supernova 1987A in the Large Magellanic Cloud from Las Campanas Observatory in Chile. Albert Jones spotted it independently in New Zealand within the same day.
Maria Margaretha Kirch was born in Panitzsch, Saxony. In 1702 she became the first person to identify the Comet of 1702 as a comet.
A total solar eclipse crossed Washington, Oregon, Idaho, Montana and North Dakota. It was the last total eclipse seen from the contiguous United States until 21 August 2017.
Alan Guth, the physicist who proposed that the early universe went through a phase of exponential expansion known as inflation, was born in New Brunswick, New Jersey.
NASA's New Horizons spacecraft made its closest approach to Jupiter, using the planet's gravity to speed its journey toward Pluto.
Charles Messier discovered the spiral galaxy M66, describing it as very long and very faint.
The second 8.2-meter unit telescope of ESO's Very Large Telescope, UT2, later named Kueyen, achieved technical first light at Paranal.
source: ESO: VLT Unit Telescopes Named at Paranal Inauguration (eso9921)

events.text: Pioneer 10 was launched. It became the first spacecraft to fly through the main asteroid belt and the first to fly past Jupiter.

Pioneer 4 was launched, becoming the first American spacecraft to leave Earth's gravity. Sent to fly near the Moon, it returned data for 82 hours and became the first American craft in orbit around the Sun.
Charles Messier added the Orion Nebula to his catalog as M42, measuring its position on the same night as several other well-known objects.
Voyager 1 made its closest approach to Jupiter, passing about 280,000 kilometers from the planet.
ESO's Paranal Observatory in Chile, home of the Very Large Telescope, was officially inaugurated.
source: ESO: VLT Unit Telescopes Named at Paranal Inauguration (eso9921)

events.text: NASA launched the Kepler space telescope, built to search for Earth-sized planets orbiting other stars.
John Herschel was born in Slough, England. He continued his father's survey of stars and nebulae, studied double stars, and later observed the southern sky.
Japan's Suisei probe made its closest approach to Halley's Comet, the second of five spacecraft to fly past the comet that month.
source: Astronomy: March 8, 1986: The second of five probes flies by Halley's Comet

events.text: William Herschel discovered the spiral galaxy NGC 2841.
Astronomers at the Space Telescope Science Institute released the Hubble Ultra Deep Field, the deepest visible-light image of the universe made up to that time, showing about 10,000 galaxies.
source: NASA: Hubble's Deepest View Ever of the Universe Unveils Earliest Galaxies

events.text: James Elliot, Edward Dunham and Jessica Mink discovered the rings of Uranus from the Kuiper Airborne Observatory, when a star they were watching blinked out several times before and after passing behind the planet.
Urbain Le Verrier was born in Saint-Lô, France. His calculations from irregularities in the orbit of Uranus led Johann Galle to find Neptune in 1846.
William Herschel discovered the spiral galaxy now known as NGC 3190, although he did not recognize its spiral structure.
The Cassini spacecraft flew past Saturn's moon Enceladus, passing directly through one of its plumes and sampling the ejected material.
William Herschel first observed Uranus, an observation that led to its discovery as a planet.
Percival Lowell was born in Boston. He founded a private observatory in Flagstaff, Arizona, and started the search for a planet beyond Neptune that led to the discovery of Pluto in 1930.
The Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) was inaugurated at an official ceremony in the Chilean Andes, marking its move from construction to a fully operational observatory.
source: ESO: ALMA Inauguration Heralds New Era of Discovery (eso1312)

events.text: The European probe Giotto flew past Halley's Comet at a distance of 596 kilometers and survived despite being hit by small particles.
Pierre Méchain discovered the galaxy M100, together with its neighbors M98 and M99.
Caroline Herschel was born in Hanover. She went on to find three nebulae in 1783 and became the first woman to discover a comet, eventually finding eight.
William Herschel introduced the term planetary nebula in a letter to Jérôme Lalande, describing a half dozen such objects whose nature was still unclear.
Friedrich Wilhelm Bessel died in Königsberg. He was the first to measure the parallax, and so the distance, of a star other than the Sun.
Charles Messier discovered and cataloged the galaxy M86, along with seven more galaxies of the Virgo Cluster and the globular cluster M92 on the same night.

The Swift satellite detected the gamma-ray burst GRB 080319B. Its afterglow reached magnitude 5.8, bright enough to be seen with the naked eye for about 30 seconds, although the explosion happened about 7.5 billion years ago.
Pierre Méchain discovered the spiral galaxies M95 and M96.
Pierre Méchain discovered NGC 5195, the dwarf galaxy interacting with the Whirlpool Galaxy.
William Herschel discovered the dwarf elliptical galaxy NGC 4489 in Coma Berenices.
The European team behind the Planck space observatory released the mission's all-sky map of the microwave background radiation.
Comet Hale-Bopp made its closest approach to Earth, passing at a distance of 1.315 astronomical units.
Pierre-Simon Laplace was born in Normandy, France. He later studied the stability of the solar system, accounting for the observed departures of the planets from their predicted orbits.
source: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Pierre-Simon, marquis de Laplace

events.text: John William Draper announced at the New York Lyceum of Natural History that he had made a successful daguerreotype of the Moon from his rooftop observatory.
source: Astronomy: March 23, 1840: The first photo of the Moon

events.text: Walter Baade was born in Germany. His discovery of two types of Cepheid variable stars led to a revision of distances in the universe that doubled its known size.
Carolyn and Eugene Shoemaker and David Levy found Comet Shoemaker-Levy 9 on two photographs taken with the 46-centimeter Schmidt telescope at Palomar Observatory.
Dutch astronomer Christiaan Huygens discovered Titan, the largest moon of Saturn.
ESO's La Silla Observatory in Chile was inaugurated, with the President of Chile, Eduardo Frei Montalva, among those attending.

Astronomers announced that the centaur Chariklo has two rings, the first rings found around an asteroid. Seven telescopes in South America had seen a star's light dip briefly before and after Chariklo passed in front of it.
Pierre Méchain discovered the spiral galaxy M101, the Pinwheel Galaxy, which became one of the last entries in Charles Messier's catalog.
German astronomer Heinrich Olbers discovered Pallas, which was considered a planet at the time.
Amateur astronomer Francisco Garcia Diaz of Lugo, Spain, discovered supernova SN 1993J in Bode's Galaxy, M81.
Heinrich Olbers discovered the asteroid Vesta in the constellation Virgo.

NASA announced that the Hubble Space Telescope had detected Earendel, the most distant single star seen so far, whose light took 12.9 billion years to reach Earth. A galaxy cluster in the foreground magnified its brightness a thousandfold or more.
source: NASA: Record Broken: Hubble Spots Farthest Star Ever Seen

events.text: Michael Brown, Chad Trujillo and David Rabinowitz discovered the dwarf planet Makemake at Palomar Observatory.
Comet Hale-Bopp passed perihelion, its closest point to the Sun, about two years after Alan Hale and Thomas Bopp discovered it.
French physicists Hippolyte Fizeau and Leon Foucault took the first photograph of the Sun, a daguerreotype that showed sunspots.
source: Astronomy: April 2, 1845, the first photo of the Sun

events.text: Joseph-Nicolas Delisle was born in Paris. The French astronomer organized a worldwide study of the 1761 transit of Venus to measure the distance to the Sun.
NASA launched the Compton Gamma Ray Observatory aboard the Space Shuttle Atlantis on mission STS-37.
William Herschel discovered the spiral galaxy NGC 4565.
NASA launched Pioneer 11 from Cape Canaveral. The probe later became the first spacecraft to encounter Saturn, flying past the planet in 1979.
NASA launched the 2001 Mars Odyssey orbiter on a Delta II rocket from Cape Canaveral.
A total solar eclipse crossed North America, with totality visible from 6 Mexican states, 15 U.S. states and 6 Canadian provinces.
Charles Messier found the globular cluster M68 and added it to his catalog.
The Event Horizon Telescope collaboration published the first image of a black hole, the one at the center of the galaxy Messier 87.
Samuel Heinrich Schwabe died in Dessau. The German amateur astronomer found after 17 years of almost daily observations that sunspots rise and fall in number over a cycle of about 10 years.
Charles Messier, the French astronomer known for his catalog of nebulae and star clusters, died in Paris at age 86.
Annie Jump Cannon died. Her work classifying stars by color, which relates to temperature, produced the OBAFGKM scheme adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 1922.
source: Astronomy: April 13, 1941, the death of Annie Jump Cannon

events.text: Christiaan Huygens, the Dutch scientist who worked out the true shape of the rings of Saturn, was born in The Hague.
Charles Messier cataloged the galaxy M58 while following the comet of 1779.
The complete camera of the Vera C. Rubin Observatory detected its first photons, which appeared as rings until the instrument was adjusted to focus them.
John Hadley was born in Hertfordshire, England. He improved the reflecting telescope and built the first one accurate and powerful enough to be useful in astronomy.
ESA and NASA released a Hubble image of 30 Doradus, a star-forming region in the heart of the Tarantula Nebula that holds several million stars.
Astronomers announced Kepler-186f, an Earth-sized planet orbiting in the habitable zone of a red dwarf star.
NASA launched the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) on a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from Cape Canaveral.
The Hubble Space Telescope marked its 23rd year in orbit with a new infrared image of the Horsehead Nebula.
The Hubble Space Telescope marked its 28th anniversary with an image of part of the Lagoon Nebula, a large stellar nursery.
Halley's Comet reached perihelion during the 1910 apparition, a month before Earth passed through its tail.
Astronomers celebrated the 21st anniversary of the Hubble Space Telescope with an image of Arp 273, a group of interacting galaxies.
Aleksander Wolszczan and Dale Frail announced proof of planets orbiting the pulsar PSR B1257+12, confirming research first published in 1992.
source: Astronomy: April 21, 1994, the discovery of exoplanets

events.text: Immanuel Kant was born. The philosopher argued that our galaxy is a wide rotating disk and was the first to suggest that some nebulae seen from Earth are other galaxies.
source: Astronomy: April 22, 1724, the birth of Immanuel Kant

events.text: ESA and NASA marked the 25th anniversary of the Hubble Space Telescope with an infrared image of Westerlund 2, a young cluster of about 3,000 stars in Carina.
The Hubble Space Telescope celebrated the 31st anniversary of its launch with an image of AG Carinae, one of the brightest stars in our galaxy.
The Space Shuttle Discovery launched the Hubble Space Telescope on mission STS-31.
The Hubble Space Telescope was deployed into orbit from the Space Shuttle Discovery, one day after its launch.
NASA and ESA marked the 15th anniversary of the Hubble Space Telescope with new views of the Eagle Nebula and the Whirlpool Galaxy, M51.
Harlow Shapley and Heber Curtis held the Great Debate at the U.S. National Museum in Washington, D.C.
William Herschel discovered the galaxy NGC 4449.
The European Space Agency announced that the SOHO spacecraft could observe the far side of the Sun, the first observatory able to do so.
source: Astronomy: April 27, 2001, SOHO sees the farside of the Sun

events.text: William Herschel discovered the galaxy NGC 4214.
Jan Oort, the Dutch astronomer who confirmed the rotation of the Milky Way and proposed a distant cloud of comets around the Sun, was born in Franeker.
The Galaxy Evolution Explorer (GALEX), an ultraviolet space telescope, was launched on a Pegasus XL rocket.
James Dunlop discovered the galaxy NGC 5128, now known as Centaurus A, during a survey at the Parramatta Observatory.
Carl Friedrich Gauss, the German mathematician whose work extended to planetary astronomy, was born in Brunswick.
Gerard Kuiper discovered Nereid, a moon of Neptune, on photographic plates taken with the 82-inch telescope at McDonald Observatory.
Astronomers using the TRAPPIST telescope at ESO's La Silla Observatory announced three planets orbiting the ultracool dwarf star TRAPPIST-1, about 40 light-years away.
source: ESO: Three Potentially Habitable Worlds Found Around Nearby Ultracool Dwarf Star (eso1615)

events.text: Charles Messier logged the globular cluster M3 in Canes Venatici, his first original discovery for his catalog.
NASA's Magellan probe was launched from Space Shuttle Atlantis, the first deep space probe launched by a shuttle. It went on to map about 98 percent of the surface of Venus.
Gottfried Kirch and Maria Margarethe Kirch first saw the globular cluster now known as M5 while they were observing a comet.
Barnaba Oriani discovered the spiral galaxy M61 in Virgo. Charles Messier saw it the same night but mistook it for a comet.
Willem de Sitter was born in Sneek, the Netherlands. He built models of the universe from general relativity and proposed that it expands.
Mercury passed across the face of the Sun. Transits in May are rarer than those in November because they happen about a month after Mercury's aphelion.
source: NASA Eclipse Web Site: Catalog of Transits of Mercury

events.text: Charles Messier cataloged the globular cluster M4 in Scorpius and was the first to resolve it into a cluster of faint stars.
Mercury crossed the face of the Sun in a transit lasting more than seven hours, and NASA's Solar Dynamics Observatory recorded it in near real time.
source: NASA Scientific Visualization Studio: Mercury Transit Live Shots May 9, 2016

events.text: James Dunlop discovered the galaxy NGC 1808 and described it as a faint nebula.
Cecilia Payne-Gaposchkin was born in Wendover, England. She went on to show that stars are made mostly of hydrogen and helium.
Pierre Méchain discovered the Sombrero Galaxy, now known as M104, in Virgo.

Space Shuttle Atlantis launched on the fifth and final servicing mission to the Hubble Space Telescope, which installed Wide Field Camera 3 and a new ultraviolet spectrograph and repaired two instruments.
Astronomers of the Event Horizon Telescope collaboration unveiled the first image of Sagittarius A*, the supermassive black hole at the center of the Milky Way.
source: ESO: Astronomers reveal first image of the black hole at the heart of our galaxy

events.text: James Dunlop discovered the globular cluster NGC 6388 using a 20 cm reflector.
John Tebbutt of Windsor, New South Wales, discovered the Great Comet of 1861 about a month before it reached perihelion.
ESA's Herschel Space Observatory and the Planck spacecraft lifted off together on an Ariane 5 rocket from the Guiana Space Center in French Guiana.
The Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument began its five-year main survey on the Nicholas U. Mayall Telescope at Kitt Peak.
Williamina Fleming was born in Dundee, Scotland. At Harvard she classified stellar spectra and found 10 novae, 52 nebulae and hundreds of variable stars.
source: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Williamina Paton Stevens Fleming

events.text: Nancy Grace Roman was born in Nashville, Tennessee. Known as the Mother of Hubble, she spent years championing the space telescope and winning its funding.
source: Astronomy: May 16, 1925, The birth of Nancy Grace Roman

events.text: Norman Lockyer was born in Rugby, England. With Pierre Janssen he is credited with discovering the gas helium.
Arthur Schuster photographed the sungrazing Comet Tewfik during a total solar eclipse, the first photograph of a comet taken during an eclipse.
source: Astronomy: May 17, 1882, Comet Tewfik is spotted during an eclipse

events.text: The Hubble Space Telescope took the second of the discovery images of Nix, a small moon of Pluto found by Max Mutchler and Andrew Steffl of the Pluto Companion Search Team.
Koichi Itagaki first observed the supernova SN 2023ixf in the Pinwheel Galaxy, M101.
The Hubble Space Telescope took its first image with the Wide Field/Planetary Camera, a view of stars around HD96755 in the open cluster NGC 3532 in Carina.
source: Space.com: Hubble Telescope Opened Its Eyes 25 Years Ago Today

events.text: Williamina Fleming died. At Harvard she discovered 10 novae, more than 50 nebulae including the Horsehead Nebula, and the first known white dwarf.
source: Astronomy: May 21, 1911, The death of Williamina Fleming

events.text: Thomas Gold was born in Vienna. He helped develop the steady-state theory of the universe.
Charles Messier independently found the globular cluster M5 in Serpens and described it as a round nebula without stars.
Nicolaus Copernicus died in Frauenburg, East Prussia, in the year his book proposing that the planets circle the Sun was published.
William Herschel discovered the elliptical galaxy NGC 5982 in Draco.
The first unit telescope of ESO's Very Large Telescope at Paranal saw first light and returned scientifically useful images on the night of 25 to 26 May.
source: ESO: First light for the VLT (eso9820)

events.text: The SOFIA airborne observatory saw first light and returned images of the core of the galaxy M82 and of heat escaping from Jupiter.
source: Wikipedia: Stratospheric Observatory for Infrared Astronomy

events.text: Astronomers at Yerkes, Harvard, Allegheny and Urbana observatories used photoelectric cells to turn light from the star Arcturus into current that lit the central building of the Chicago World's Fair.
source: University of Chicago Library: Yerkes Observatory at the Century of Progress 1933 World's Fair

events.text: James Dunlop discovered the spiral galaxy NGC 1566, later known as the Spanish Dancer.
Frank Drake was born in Chicago. He devised the Drake equation and led Project Ozma, the first systematic search for radio signals from other civilizations.
Charles Messier discovered the globular cluster M10 in Ophiuchus and entered it as number 10 in his list.
Expeditions to Principe and Sobral in Brazil observed a total solar eclipse to test Einstein's prediction that the Sun's gravity bends starlight.
Charles Messier discovered the globular cluster M12 in Ophiuchus and described it as a nebula without stars.
Martin Schwarzschild was born in Potsdam. He studied stellar structure and red giants and led the Stratoscope balloon telescope projects.
Charles Messier added the Hercules globular cluster M13 to his catalog. Edmond Halley had discovered the cluster in 1714.
The X-ray satellite ROSAT launched on a Delta II rocket from Cape Canaveral. Its six-month all-sky survey cataloged more than 150,000 X-ray objects.
ESA launched Mars Express, the first planetary mission the agency attempted.
The 200-inch Hale Telescope was dedicated at Palomar Observatory in California and named after George Ellery Hale, whose widow attended the ceremony.
Chad Trujillo and Michael Brown discovered the Kuiper belt object Quaoar, now classed as a ringed dwarf planet, with the 1.22-meter Samuel Oschin telescope at Palomar Observatory.
Charles Messier discovered and cataloged the open star cluster M21 in Sagittarius.
Charles Messier discovered the Trifid Nebula, which became number 20 in his catalog.
John Couch Adams was born in Laneast, Cornwall. He is known for his part in the discovery of Neptune.
Venus crossed the face of the Sun. Expeditions from Britain, Austria and France traveled as far as Siberia, Newfoundland and Madagascar to time the transit and measure the solar parallax.
Charles Messier discovered the globular cluster M62, which he listed as the 62nd entry in his catalog.
Giovanni Domenico Cassini was born in Perinaldo. He discovered four moons of Saturn and the gap in Saturn's rings now called the Cassini Division.
ESO released the first images from the VLT Survey Telescope at Paranal Observatory, showing the star-forming region Messier 17 and the globular cluster Omega Centauri.
source: ESO: First images from the VLT Survey Telescope (eso1119)

events.text: Johann Gottfried Galle was born in Radis, Prussia. In 1846 he became the first person to view and identify the planet Neptune.
Eugene Parker was born in Houghton, Michigan. In 1958 he proposed the existence of the solar wind, a stream of charged particles flowing from the Sun.
source: Astronomy: June 10, 1927, The birth of Eugene Parker

events.text: NASA launched the Gamma-ray Large Area Space Telescope, later renamed the Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope, to study pulsars, gamma-ray bursts and supermassive black holes.
Japanese amateur astronomer Seiji Ueda discovered Nova Herculis 2021, also known as V1674 Herculis. It faded from peak brightness in just over a day, making it the fastest nova ever recorded.
source: Astronomy: June 12, 2021, Seiji Ueda discovers Nova Herculis 2021

events.text: NASA launched NuSTAR, the first satellite to focus high-energy X-rays.
Charles Messier verified the Sunflower Galaxy, M63, which his colleague Pierre Méchain had found first.
A solar eclipse recorded by Assyrian scribes took place. Dated to 15 June 763 BC in the proleptic Julian calendar, it anchors the absolute chronology of the ancient Near East for the Assyrian period.
LIGO announced its second detection of gravitational waves, from two black holes of about 14 and 8 solar masses that merged some 1.4 billion light-years away.
source: LIGO Caltech: second gravitational-wave detection announced (news release, 15 June 2016)

events.text: Stephen Synnott discovered Neptune's moon Proteus in images taken by Voyager 2 as it approached Neptune.
ESA sent the last command to the Herschel Space Observatory from its control center in Darmstadt, ending the mission's operations.
William Lassell was born in Bolton, England. With telescopes he built himself, he discovered Neptune's moon Triton and the Uranian moons Ariel and Umbriel.
Milton Humason died. Working with Edwin Hubble, he measured the redshifts of galaxies that gave evidence for the expansion of the universe.
Roy Tucker, David Tholen and Fabrizio Bernardi discovered the near-Earth asteroid Apophis at Kitt Peak National Observatory in Arizona.
Georges Lemaître died in Leuven, Belgium. He formulated the first version of the Big Bang theory, describing the universe as expanding from a primeval atom.
Max Wolf was born in Heidelberg. A pioneer of astrophotography, he discovered 248 asteroids, including the first Trojan asteroid, 588 Achilles.
William Wilson Morgan died. He used distances to O and B type stars to show that the Milky Way has spiral arms, and with Philip Keenan developed the MK system of stellar classification.
King Charles II founded the Royal Observatory at Greenwich to solve the problem of finding longitude at sea.
source: Astronomy: June 22, 1675, The Royal Observatory Greenwich is founded

events.text: James Christy of the United States Naval Observatory discovered Charon, the largest moon of Pluto, after noticing a periodic bulge on photographic plates of Pluto.
The Vera C. Rubin Observatory released its first images, including views of the Trifid and Lagoon nebulae and the Virgo Cluster, made in just over 10 hours of test observations.
source: NOIRLab: First Imagery From NSF–DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory (noirlab2521)

events.text: William Huggins captured the first photographic spectrum of a comet. Later analysis of the plate showed emission from cyanogen.
source: Astronomy: June 24, 1881, First photographic spectrum of a comet

events.text: Walter Baade died in Göttingen. He divided stars into Population I and Population II after resolving stars in the center of the Andromeda Galaxy, and with Fritz Zwicky identified supernovae as a class of objects.
Charles Messier was born in Badonviller, France. He published a catalog of 110 nebulae and star clusters, now known as the Messier objects.
Lyman Spitzer was born in Toledo, Ohio. In 1946 he proposed placing telescopes in space, and NASA's Spitzer Space Telescope is named after him.
Heber Curtis was born in Muskegon, Michigan. He argued that galaxies exist beyond the Milky Way in the 1920 Shapley and Curtis debate.
NASA decommissioned the Galaxy Evolution Explorer, GALEX, an ultraviolet space telescope launched in 2003.

George Ellery Hale was born in Chicago. He led the planning and construction of the Yerkes 40-inch refractor, the 60-inch and 100-inch telescopes at Mount Wilson and the 200-inch Hale Telescope at Palomar.
A stony asteroid about 50 to 60 meters wide exploded in the air over the East Siberian taiga, felling trees across an area of about 2,150 square kilometers. It became known as the Tunguska event.
NASA launched the Wilkinson Microwave Anisotropy Probe, WMAP, which measured tiny temperature variations in the microwave background radiation to map conditions in the early universe.
ESA's Euclid space telescope launched on a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from Cape Canaveral, Florida.
ESA launched the Giotto probe on an Ariane 1 rocket from Kourou, French Guiana. It flew past Halley's Comet the following March at a distance of 596 km.
NASA launched the CONTOUR probe to visit comets Encke and Schwassmann-Wachmann 3. The spacecraft was lost during an engine burn the following month.
Henrietta Swan Leavitt was born. She discovered the relation between the luminosity and the period of Cepheid variable stars, which gave astronomers a way to measure distances to faraway galaxies.
The impactor released by NASA's Deep Impact spacecraft struck Comet Tempel 1.
Isaac Newton's Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica was published. The Latin work, financed by Edmond Halley, set out laws of motion that explained both earthly and celestial physics.
source: Astronomy: July 5, 1687, Newton's Principia is published

events.text: The longest total lunar eclipse of the 20th century took place, with totality lasting 1 hour 45 minutes. It was visible from Australia, the Pacific, the Americas and western Africa.
source: Astronomy: July 6, 1982, The longest total lunar eclipse of the century

events.text: NASA launched the Opportunity rover to Mars. It found geological and mineral evidence that Mars once had water and kept working until 2018.
Christiaan Huygens died in The Hague. He identified Saturn's moon Titan and explained the planet's odd appearance as a thin, flat ring.
Voyager 2 made its closest approach to Jupiter.
Johann Gottfried Galle died in Potsdam at 98. In 1846 he was the first person to see and identify the planet Neptune.
Japan launched the X-ray astronomy satellite Suzaku on an M-V rocket from the Uchinoura Space Center.
A total solar eclipse crossed Mexico with totality lasting up to 6 minutes and 53 seconds. No longer total eclipse will occur until 2132.
U.S. President Joe Biden unveiled Webb's First Deep Field, the first full false-color image from the James Webb Space Telescope.
Charles Messier discovered the Dumbbell Nebula in Vulpecula, the first planetary nebula ever found. It became number 27 in his catalog.
The first full-color images from the James Webb Space Telescope were released, including the Carina Nebula, Stephan's Quintet, the Southern Ring Nebula and the galaxy cluster SMACS 0723.
The Gran Telescopio Canarias began its first observations at Roque de los Muchachos Observatory on La Palma, using 12 segments of its 10.4-meter primary mirror.
The Spektr-RG X-ray observatory launched on a Proton-M rocket from Baikonur, carrying the German eROSITA telescope and the Russian ART-XC telescope.
NASA's New Horizons spacecraft made its closest approach to Pluto, passing 12,472 km from the surface.
Jocelyn Bell Burnell was born. As a doctoral student at Cambridge in 1967 she discovered the first pulsars.
Lewis Swift discovered the comet later named Swift-Tuttle, the parent body of the Perseid meteor shower. Horace Tuttle found it independently three days later.
Fragment A of Comet Shoemaker-Levy 9 struck Jupiter's southern hemisphere, the first of a series of impacts that continued until July 22.
William Bond and John Adams Whipple photographed Vega at Harvard College Observatory with a daguerreotype, making it the first star other than the Sun to be photographed.
Eugene Shoemaker, co-discoverer of Comet Shoemaker-Levy 9, died in a car crash in central Australia while searching for impact craters.
Edward Charles Pickering was born. He directed Harvard College Observatory from 1877 until his death in 1919.
NASA's Cassini spacecraft imaged Saturn and most of its rings, with Earth and the Moon showing as distant pale dots. The picture became known as The Day the Earth Smiled.
source: Wikipedia: The Day the Earth Smiled

events.text: The Viking 1 lander touched down in Chryse Planitia, the first successful landing on Mars.
Jean Picard was born in La Flèche, France. He is best known for measuring the size of the Earth by surveying one degree of latitude along the Paris Meridian.
Friedrich Wilhelm Bessel was born. In 1838 he published a parallax for the star 61 Cygni, making him the first astronomer to determine a reliable distance to a star.
The longest total solar eclipse of the 21st century crossed India, China and the Pacific, with totality lasting up to 6 minutes and 38 seconds.
Vera Rubin was born in Philadelphia. Her measurements of how fast galaxies rotate provided evidence for dark matter.
Alan Hale and Thomas Bopp independently discovered Comet Hale-Bopp, Hale from his driveway in New Mexico and Bopp near Phoenix, Arizona.
NASA launched the Chandra X-ray Observatory, which became the agency's flagship mission for X-ray astronomy.
Charles Messier discovered the globular cluster Messier 54 in Sagittarius.
Chushiro Hayashi was born. His models of how stars form identified the Hayashi phase, a stage when a newborn star is extremely bright and active.
source: Astronomy: July 25, 1920, The birth of Chushiro Hayashi

events.text: Comet LINEAR, C/1999 S4, began to break apart. The fragmentation continued through mid-August until nothing of the comet remained visible.
Charles Messier discovered the globular cluster Messier 28 in the upper part of the bow of Sagittarius.
George Biddell Airy was born. He served as Astronomer Royal from 1835 to 1881.

Julius Berkowski photographed a total solar eclipse from the Royal Observatory in Königsberg, Prussia. His 84-second daguerreotype was the earliest scientifically useful photograph of a total eclipse.
A total solar eclipse crossed the western United States. Many leading astronomers observed it from high in the Rocky Mountains, including Pikes Peak in Colorado.
Mike Brown, Chad Trujillo and David Rabinowitz announced the discovery of the dwarf planet now named Eris, found in images taken with the Samuel Oschin telescope at Palomar Observatory.
Galileo Galilei observed Saturn with a telescope and thought the planet had two moons, one on either side. He was actually seeing its rings.
source: Astronomy: July 30, 1610, Galileo sees Saturn's rings

events.text: Ranger 7 crashed into the Moon as planned after sending back more than 4,300 photographs in the last 17 minutes of its flight. The final frames showed features about half a meter across.
Caroline Herschel discovered her first comet while using her brother William's telescope during his absence. She went on to find eight comets by 1797.
Maria Mitchell was born on Nantucket, Massachusetts. Her work on a new comet in 1847, known as Miss Mitchell's Comet, brought her international recognition.
Charles Messier cataloged the globular cluster M30 in Capricornus, one of his own original discoveries.
NASA's Juno spacecraft launched from Cape Canaveral on a five-year journey to Jupiter, where it entered orbit in July 2016.
ESA's Rosetta spacecraft reached comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko and began a series of maneuvers to fly around it at distances of 10 to 30 kilometers.

A total solar eclipse crossed the United States and became the first major eclipse to be photographed. Maria Mitchell took a group of Vassar College students to observe it with telescopes in Burlington, Iowa.
ESA launched Hipparcos, the first space experiment devoted to precision astrometry, the accurate measurement of the positions and distances of stars and other celestial objects.
William Fowler was born in Pittsburgh. With Fred Hoyle and other colleagues he developed a widely accepted theory of how nuclear reactions in stars produce the chemical elements.
Charles Messier observed the small elliptical galaxy now known as M110, a companion of the Andromeda Galaxy. He never entered it in his catalog, and it was added to the list in 1966.

A total solar eclipse crossed southern England, France, Germany and other countries on its way to the Bay of Bengal. It was the first total eclipse visible in the United Kingdom since 1927 and one of the most viewed in history.
NASA launched the Parker Solar Probe, a mission built to fly closer to the Sun than any spacecraft before it.
Gustav Witt at the Urania Observatory in Berlin discovered the asteroid 433 Eros. Auguste Charlois found it independently at Nice on the same day.
The satellite Explorer 6 took the first image of Earth ever made by a satellite.

Ohio State University's Big Ear radio telescope recorded a strong narrowband radio signal that became known as the Wow! signal. Astronomer Jerry Ehman found it a few days later while reviewing the data.
Pierre Méchain was born in Laon, France. He discovered eleven comets and found many of the nebulae that Charles Messier added to his catalog.
Both LIGO detectors recorded gravitational waves from two neutron stars colliding about 130 million light-years away. Observatories then saw light from the same event, from gamma rays to radio waves.

Pierre Janssen observed a total solar eclipse from Guntur in India and noticed a bright yellow line in the spectrum of solar prominences that could not come from sodium. The line led to the discovery of the element helium.
John Flamsteed, the first Astronomer Royal of England, was born near Derby. His catalog of about 3,000 stars gave many stars the Flamsteed numbers still used today.
The Chandra X-ray Observatory took its official first light image, a one-hour observation of the supernova remnant Cassiopeia A.
source: Chandra X-ray Center: First Light Image of Cassiopeia A

events.text: Ernst Hartwig at Dorpat Observatory in Estonia detected the supernova S Andromedae in the Andromeda Galaxy. He is credited as its discoverer.
Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar died in Chicago. He shared the 1983 Nobel Prize in Physics for work on the late stages in the evolution of massive stars.
Samuel Pierpont Langley was born in Roxbury, Massachusetts. As director of the Allegheny Observatory he invented the bolometer, which carried solar studies into the infrared.
NASA's Lunar Orbiter 1 took the first image of Earth from the distance of the Moon.
The Palomar Transient Factory survey discovered the supernova SN 2011fe in the Pinwheel Galaxy, Messier 101.
Charles Messier cataloged the Triangulum Galaxy as M33. Giovanni Battista Hodierna had probably seen it before 1654.
NASA launched the Spitzer Space Telescope, an infrared observatory that operated until engineers decommissioned it in January 2020.
Johann Franz Encke died in Spandau. He worked out the orbital period of the comet that now carries his name and calculated the solar parallax from the Venus transits of 1761 and 1769.
Caroline Herschel independently discovered the galaxy M110, about ten years after Charles Messier first saw it, and listed it as No. 9 on her own list.
Charles Messier, while following a comet, found a nebulous patch in Taurus that looked like a comet. The object, the Crab Nebula, became the first entry in his catalog as M1.
William Herschel discovered Enceladus, one of the moons of Saturn.
Pierre Méchain discovered the globular cluster M72 in Aquarius. Charles Messier later observed it and added it to his catalog.
Charles Messier cataloged the open cluster M35 in Gemini and credited John Bevis with finding it earlier.
Charles Messier discovered two globular clusters in southern Sagittarius, M69 and M70.
Karl Ludwig Harding discovered Juno, the third asteroid ever found.
English astronomers Richard Carrington and Richard Hodgson independently recorded the earliest observations of a solar flare, a bright patch that moved across the Sun for about five minutes.
Pioneer 11 made its closest approach to Saturn, becoming the first probe to encounter the planet.
Scottish astronomer James Dunlop discovered the barred spiral galaxy NGC 1365 in the southern constellation Fornax.
James Dunlop discovered the lenticular galaxy NGC 1316, which is also the radio source Fornax A.
YEPUN, the fourth Unit Telescope of ESO's Very Large Telescope at Paranal, saw first light. Its first image showed a dense Milky Way field containing the planetary nebula Hen 2-428.
source: ESO: Fourth Light at Paranal! VLT YEPUN Joins ANTU, KUEYEN and MELIPAL

events.text: William Herschel discovered the Veil Nebula, the remains of a supernova in the constellation Cygnus.
NASA launched Voyager 1, which went on to fly past Jupiter and Saturn and later sent back the images behind the Pale Blue Dot.
Brett Gladman, Philip Nicholson, Joseph Burns and John Kavelaars discovered Caliban and Sycorax, two irregular moons of Uranus, with the 200-inch Hale Telescope.
Charles Messier cataloged the open cluster M52 while following the comet of that year, which passed close to it.
William Herschel discovered the planetary nebula NGC 7009, later called the Saturn Nebula, with a telescope of his own design in his garden at Datchet, England.
NASA launched OSIRIS-REx, a mission to collect a sample from a near-Earth asteroid and bring it back to Earth.
William Herschel discovered the spiral galaxy NGC 6946, now known as the Fireworks Galaxy.
Edward Emerson Barnard discovered Amalthea, a small inner moon of Jupiter, with the 36-inch refractor at Lick Observatory.

James Edward Keeler was born. His spectra of Saturn's rings showed that different parts orbit at different speeds, and his work with the Crossley reflector at Lick Observatory advanced the study of nebulae.
Jean-Dominique Maraldi discovered the globular cluster M2. Charles Messier found it again on the same date in 1760 and described it as a nebula without stars.
Charles Messier cataloged the Crab Nebula as the first entry in his list. He had come across it in August while searching for the predicted return of Halley's Comet.
The 570-megapixel Dark Energy Camera took its first pictures of the southern sky from the Victor M. Blanco telescope at Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory in Chile.
source: Fermilab: World's most powerful digital camera opens eye, records first images in hunt for dark energy

events.text: The Soviet probe Luna 2 struck the Moon, the first spacecraft to touch the surface of the Moon and the first human-made object to reach another celestial body.
Giovanni Domenico Cassini died in Paris. He discovered four moons of Saturn, Iapetus, Rhea, Tethys and Dione, and the gap in Saturn's rings now called the Cassini Division.

The two LIGO detectors in Hanford, Washington, and Livingston, Louisiana, recorded GW150914, the first direct observation of gravitational waves. The signal came from the merger of two black holes of about 35 and 30 solar masses.
source: Wikipedia: First observation of gravitational waves

events.text: NASA's Cassini spacecraft ended its mission by entering Saturn's upper atmosphere, where it burned up after nearly 20 years in space.
Russian mathematician Alexander Friedmann died. In 1922 he introduced the idea of an expanding universe filled with moving matter.
William Herschel discovered Mimas, a moon of Saturn, with his 40-foot reflecting telescope.
British astronomer John Herschel discovered the galaxy NGC 7714.
Japanese amateur astronomers Kaoru Ikeya and Tsutomu Seki independently discovered the sungrazing comet Ikeya-Seki within about 15 minutes of each other.

French astronomer Jean-Baptiste Delambre was born in Amiens. He compiled tables of the motions of Jupiter's satellites and led the northern expedition that measured the meridian from Dunkirk to Rodez.
French astronomer Pierre Méchain died in Castellón de la Plana, Spain. He discovered about 25 deep-sky objects and eight comets and worked closely with Charles Messier.
The Galileo spacecraft was deliberately sent into Jupiter's atmosphere and destroyed, so that it could not contaminate any of Jupiter's moons.
Vitaly Nevsky and Artyom Novichonok discovered Comet ISON with a 0.4-meter reflector of the International Scientific Optical Network. The comet broke apart near the Sun in late 2013.
Saul Perlmutter was born. He shared the 2011 Nobel Prize in Physics for evidence that the expansion of the universe is accelerating.
Caroline Herschel discovered the Sculptor Galaxy, NGC 253, with a small Newtonian telescope she used to sweep the sky for comets.
Johann Gottfried Galle observed Neptune through a telescope at the Berlin Observatory, close to the position Urbain Le Verrier had predicted from its pull on Uranus.
William Herschel discovered the globular cluster NGC 6934.
The OSIRIS-REx sample capsule landed back on Earth carrying material collected from the asteroid Bennu.
Astronomers released the Hubble eXtreme Deep Field, built from about 23 days of Hubble exposures collected over 10 years. The image contains about 5,500 galaxies.
NASA's DART spacecraft struck the small asteroid moonlet Dimorphos on purpose. The collision shortened its orbit around Didymos by 32 minutes.
Scottish astronomer James Dunlop discovered the irregular galaxy NGC 1313, sometimes called the Topsy Turvy Galaxy.
NASA launched the Dawn spacecraft to the asteroid belt. It later orbited Vesta and Ceres, the first spacecraft to orbit two separate bodies beyond Earth.
James Dunlop discovered the barred spiral galaxy NGC 1433.
Edwin Hubble died in San Marino, California. He showed that many nebulae are galaxies beyond the Milky Way and found that more distant galaxies recede faster, evidence that the universe is expanding.
India launched AstroSat, its first dedicated space observatory for observing the sky across several wavelengths.

The small near-Earth asteroid 2024 PT5 became temporarily captured by Earth's gravity, a state that lasted until 25 November. The ATLAS survey station at Sutherland, South Africa, had discovered it in August.
Henry Draper took the first photograph of the Orion Nebula, a 50-minute exposure with his 11-inch Clark refractor.
ESA's Rosetta spacecraft ended its mission by landing hard on comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko in the comet's Ma'at region.
Maria Mitchell slipped out of a party, went up to her roof to observe, and discovered a new comet.
source: APS News: October 1847, Maria Mitchell Discovers a Comet

events.text: Hans Lipperhey filed for a 30-year patent from the States General of the Netherlands for an instrument for seeing things far away as if they were near, the first written record of a telescope.
source: AAS: This Month in Astronomical History, The Invention of the Telescope

events.text: Max Wolf died. The German astronomer founded and directed the Königstuhl Observatory and used photography to discover asteroids.
John Herschel first observed NGC 7090, a spiral galaxy in the southern constellation Indus that is seen edge-on from Earth.
Saul Perlmutter, Brian Schmidt and Adam Riess were awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for discovering, through observations of distant supernovae, that the expansion of the universe is accelerating.
source: Nobel Prize: The Nobel Prize in Physics 2011, press release

events.text: Belgium, Germany, France, the Netherlands and Sweden signed the convention that established the European Southern Observatory.
William Herschel discovered NGC 891, a spiral galaxy in Andromeda seen almost exactly edge-on.
Michel Mayor and Didier Queloz of the University of Geneva announced the discovery of 51 Pegasi b, a planet orbiting a Sun-like star.
The Soviet probe Luna 3 photographed the far side of the Moon.
Ejnar Hertzsprung was born in Copenhagen. He is best remembered for his role in developing the Hertzsprung-Russell diagram of stars.
Lodovico delle Colombe made the first recorded European observation of the supernova now known as Kepler's Supernova, SN 1604.
William Herschel discovered the barred spiral galaxy NGC 1073.
William Herschel discovered NGC 1097, a barred spiral galaxy in the southern constellation Fornax.
William Lassell discovered Triton, the largest moon of Neptune, just 17 days after Neptune itself was found.
Heinrich Wilhelm Olbers was born in Arbergen. He later discovered the asteroids Pallas and Vesta.
The Large Binocular Telescope saw first light with a single primary mirror, observing the edge-on galaxy NGC 891.
Charles Messier discovered the Whirlpool Galaxy, M51, while observing a comet, and described it as a very faint nebula without stars.
Martin Ryle died. The English radio astronomer pioneered aperture synthesis and received the 1974 Nobel Prize in Physics.
The Cassini spacecraft launched on its mission to Saturn.
NASA announced that its missions had detected light from a gravitational-wave event, the merger of two neutron stars in the galaxy NGC 4993 about 130 million light-years away.
source: NASA: NASA Missions Catch First Light from a Gravitational-Wave Event

events.text: William Herschel discovered NGC 1275, a galaxy in the constellation Perseus.
ESA's INTEGRAL gamma-ray observatory was launched.
Space shuttle Atlantis carried the Galileo spacecraft into Earth orbit at the start of its journey to Jupiter.
Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar was born in Lahore. He is known for the Chandrasekhar limit, the maximum mass of a white dwarf star.
Robert Weryk discovered ʻOumuamua, the first known interstellar object, using the Pan-STARRS telescope at Haleakalā Observatory in Hawaii.
The James Webb Space Telescope's view of the Pillars of Creation in the Eagle Nebula was released, showing dense clouds of gas and dust where new stars are forming.
source: ESA/Webb: NASA's Webb Takes Star-Filled Portrait of Pillars of Creation (weic2216)

events.text: William Herschel discovered the spiral galaxy NGC 1232 in the constellation Eridanus.
Yerkes Observatory was dedicated. It housed a 40-inch refracting telescope.
The Soviet lander Venera 9 touched down on Venus and sent back the first television pictures from the surface of another planet.
Ernst Öpik was born. The Estonian astronomer studied meteors and made the first prediction of a cloud of cometary bodies around the Solar System, later known as the Oort Cloud.
William Lassell discovered Ariel and Umbriel, two moons of Uranus.
Giovanni Cassini discovered Iapetus, a moon of Saturn.
Henry Norris Russell was born in Oyster Bay, New York. He developed the Hertzsprung-Russell diagram alongside Ejnar Hertzsprung.
Pierre Méchain found the globular cluster M79 and reported the discovery to his colleague Charles Messier.
Ulugh Beg died in Samarkand. He built the Ulugh Beg Observatory and compiled a catalog of 994 stars.

Harvard professor Samuel Williams led an expedition behind British lines to observe a solar eclipse from Long Island in present-day Maine. His description is likely the first recorded observation of Baily's Beads.
source: American Academy of Arts and Sciences: Expedition Behind Enemy Lines

events.text: Karl Reinmuth discovered the asteroid Hermes in images taken at Heidelberg Observatory.
Guillaume Le Gentil discovered M32, a small companion of the Andromeda Galaxy, while observing Andromeda with an 18-foot telescope.
Pierre Méchain discovered M77, a galaxy in Cetus that he described as a cluster of small stars containing some nebulosity.
source: Universe Today: Messier 77, the Cetus A Barred Spiral Galaxy

events.text: James Dunlop discovered NGC 1532, an edge-on barred spiral galaxy in the constellation Eridanus.
NASA retired the Kepler space telescope after it ran out of fuel. Kepler left a legacy of more than 2,600 planet discoveries outside our solar system.
source: NASA: NASA Retires Kepler Space Telescope, Passes Planet-Hunting Torch

events.text: Astronomers using the Hubble Space Telescope reported evidence of two possible new moons around Pluto, provisionally named S/2005 P1 and S/2005 P2.
source: NASA Science: NASA's Hubble Reveals Possible New Moons Around Pluto

events.text: The Arecibo radio telescope in Puerto Rico held its official opening as the Arecibo Ionospheric Observatory.
Harlow Shapley was born in Nashville, Missouri. He used Cepheid variables in globular clusters to show that the Milky Way was far larger than thought and that the Sun sits far from its center.
William Herschel discovered NGC 7635, the Bubble Nebula in Cassiopeia.
NASA's EPOXI mission flew past comet Hartley 2, coming within about 694 kilometers of it.
James Dunlop discovered the galaxy NGC 1672.
Fred Whipple was born in Red Oak, Iowa. His 1950 icy conglomerate model, known as the dirty snowball, changed how astronomers understood comets.
James Dunlop discovered the galaxy NGC 1559.

Results from the May 1919 solar eclipse expeditions were announced at a joint meeting of the Royal Society and the Royal Astronomical Society. The measured bending of starlight supported Einstein's general relativity.
Chile was chosen as the site for the ESO observatory, and the agreement between Chile and ESO was signed.
Pierre Gassendi made the first recorded observation of a transit of Mercury. He was surprised at how small the planet looked against the Sun.
The ESO 3.6-meter telescope at La Silla saw first light.
Edmond Halley was born in Haggerston, England. He predicted that the comet seen in 1682 would return in 1758, and it now bears his name.
Carl Sagan was born in Brooklyn, New York. He worked on the Pioneer and Voyager missions and co-wrote and narrated the television series Cosmos.
Tycho Brahe saw a bright new star in Cassiopeia from Herrevad Abbey. The object is now known as the supernova SN 1572.
Vesto Slipher was born in Mulberry, Indiana. At Lowell Observatory he was the first to observe the redshifts of galaxies, and his early targets included the Andromeda Nebula.
Voyager 1 made its closest approach to Saturn, passing its largest moon Titan on the same day.
ESA's Philae lander touched down on comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko. After bouncing twice it made the first soft landing on a comet nucleus.
William Herschel discovered the planetary nebula NGC 1514 in Taurus. The single star wrapped in glowing haze convinced him that some nebulosity was not made of stars.
The Einstein Observatory launched from Cape Canaveral on an Atlas-Centaur rocket. It was the first fully imaging X-ray telescope put into space.
Gottfried Kirch discovered the Great Comet of 1680 from Coburg. It was the first comet discovered with a telescope.
NASA's Mariner 9 entered orbit around Mars and became the first spacecraft to orbit another planet.
Johannes Kepler died in Regensburg, where he had traveled to collect money owed to him by the Imperial treasury.
William Herschel was born in Hanover. He later discovered Uranus and cataloged thousands of nebulae and star clusters.
The Arecibo Telescope broadcast the Arecibo message toward the globular cluster M13 at a ceremony marking the telescope's remodeling.
The Soviet Lunokhod 1 landed in Mare Imbrium and became the first robotic rover on the Moon.

NASA launched the COBE satellite from Vandenberg Air Force Base. It found that the microwave background radiation has a near-perfect black-body spectrum and detected faint variations in it, results that supported the Big Bang theory.
Edwin Hubble was born in Marshfield, Missouri. He showed that many nebulae are galaxies beyond the Milky Way and found evidence that the universe is expanding.
The Danish 1.5-meter telescope at ESO's La Silla Observatory saw first light.
NASA's Swift observatory launched on a Delta II rocket from Cape Canaveral to study gamma-ray bursts and their afterglows.
Arthur Eddington died in Cambridge. He modeled the interiors of stars and led the 1919 eclipse expedition to Principe that tested general relativity.
The New York Times reported Edwin Hubble's finding that spiral nebulae such as Andromeda are stellar systems like our own. He had measured their distances using Cepheid variable stars.
James Dunlop discovered the galaxy NGC 1317.
The Keck I telescope on Mauna Kea saw first light, with nine of its eventual 36 mirror segments in place.
Albert Einstein presented the field equations of general relativity to the Prussian Academy of Sciences in Berlin.
Nicolas-Claude Fabri de Peiresc recorded the Orion Nebula through a refracting telescope. He is generally credited as the first to notice its diffuse, nebulous nature.
Anders Celsius was born in Uppsala. As professor of astronomy there he founded the Uppsala Astronomical Observatory and linked the aurora to changes in Earth's magnetic field.
William Herschel discovered NGC 246, the planetary nebula in Cetus now known as the Skull Nebula.
Jocelyn Bell Burnell discovered PSR B1919+21, the first radio pulsar ever found.
Christian Doppler was born in Salzburg. In 1842 he described how the observed frequency of a wave depends on the motion of source and observer, using the colors of double stars as his example.
The ESO 1-meter telescope at La Silla saw first light. It was the first telescope ESO used in Chile.
The receiver platform of the Arecibo Telescope in Puerto Rico collapsed into the dish after a second main cable from one of its towers failed.
Space Shuttle Endeavor launched from Kennedy Space Center on STS-61, the first servicing mission to the Hubble Space Telescope.
NASA's Pioneer 10 made its closest approach to Jupiter, completing the first mission to the planet.
Jeremiah Horrocks observed Venus crossing the face of the Sun from Much Hoole in England. The source gives the date as 24 November in the Julian calendar and 4 December in the Gregorian calendar.
Astronomers announced Kepler-22b, the first known transiting planet found orbiting in the habitable zone of a Sun-like star.
Venus crossed the face of the Sun in the second and last transit of the 19th century, observed by expeditions sent out by several nations.
Gerard Kuiper was born in Tuitjenhorn in the Netherlands. He discovered Miranda, a moon of Uranus, and Nereid, a moon of Neptune.
NASA's Galileo spacecraft arrived at Jupiter after gravity assist flybys of Venus and Earth.
NASA's Galileo spacecraft made its first flyby of Earth on its way to Jupiter, passing 960 kilometers above the surface.
source: Astronomy: Dec. 8, 1990 & 1992, Galileo flies by Earth (twice)

events.text: Venus passed across the Sun in the first of the two transits of the 19th century. Nations sent expeditions around the world to time it and measure the astronomical unit.
The European Space Agency launched the X-ray observatory XMM-Newton on an Ariane 5 rocket from the Guiana Space Center.
Annie Jump Cannon was born in Dover, Delaware. She developed the Harvard scheme for classifying stars by their spectra and classified about 350,000 stars herself.
ESO released the first pictures from VISTA, its new infrared survey telescope at Paranal Observatory, after formally accepting the telescope the day before.
source: ESO: VISTA, pioneering new survey telescope starts work (eso0949)

events.text: Henrietta Swan Leavitt died in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Her period-luminosity relation for Cepheid variable stars gave astronomers a way to measure distances far beyond the reach of parallax.
Uhuru, the first satellite launched specifically for X-ray astronomy, lifted off from the San Marco platform off the coast of Kenya.

Albert Michelson and Francis Pease measured the angular diameter of Betelgeuse with an interferometer on the 2.5-meter telescope at Mount Wilson, the first such measurement for a star outside the Solar System.
J. P. M. Prentice discovered Nova Herculis 1934, now known as DQ Herculis, from Stowmarket in Suffolk.
Tycho Brahe, the Danish astronomer, was born.
NASA's Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer (WISE) launched on a Delta II rocket.
Audouin Dollfus identified Janus, a small inner moon of Saturn, which received the temporary designation S/1966 S 2.
Edward Emerson Barnard was born in Nashville, Tennessee. He discovered Jupiter's moon Amalthea and photographed and cataloged the dark nebulae of the Milky Way.
The Arecibo Observatory captured radar images of the asteroid 3200 Phaethon during its flyby. The images showed a spheroidal shape and a depression near its equator.
source: Astronomy: Dec. 17, 2017, Arecibo images a near-Earth asteroid

events.text: The Hubble Space Telescope began ten days of observations of a small patch of sky, taking 342 images that became the Hubble Deep Field.
ESA's Gaia spacecraft launched on a Soyuz rocket from Kourou in French Guiana.
Carl Sagan died in Seattle at the age of 62.
Jupiter and Saturn passed within 6 arcminutes of each other in a great conjunction, the closest pairing of the two planets since 1623.
Max Wolf discovered the asteroid 323 Brucia, the first asteroid found by photography.
Giovanni Domenico Cassini discovered Rhea, a moon of Saturn, using a 10.4-meter telescope made by Giuseppe Campani.
Astronaut William Anders photographed the Earth rising over the Moon from lunar orbit during Apollo 8. The picture became known as Earthrise.
Johann Georg Palitzsch, a German farmer and amateur astronomer, sighted the returning Halley's Comet, confirming Edmond Halley's prediction.
Vera Rubin died in Princeton, New Jersey. Her measurements of how fast galaxies rotate gave strong evidence for dark matter.
The James Webb Space Telescope launched on an Ariane 5 rocket from the Guiana Space Center in French Guiana.
William Herschel made the first recorded observation of NGC 2261, the nebula later known as Hubble's Variable Nebula.
Johannes Kepler was born in Weil der Stadt, Württemberg, in Germany.
Galileo observed and drew Neptune while watching Jupiter, but he took it for a fixed star.
Arthur Eddington was born in Kendal, England. He led the 1919 eclipse expedition to Príncipe that tested Einstein's theory of general relativity.
Isaac Roberts photographed the Andromeda nebula with his 20-inch reflecting telescope, and the plate showed its spiral structure.
John N. Bahcall was born in Shreveport, Louisiana. He worked for decades on the solar neutrino problem and helped develop the Hubble Space Telescope with Lyman Spitzer Jr.
Johann Elert Bode discovered the spiral galaxy M81.
